html:
The building of the TAZARA Railway by China between 1970 and 1975, a line of about 1,860 km from the copper belt of Zambia to the port of Dar es Salaam in Tanzania.

Zambia's copper had gone out by rail through white-ruled Rhodesia, South Africa and Portuguese colonies. After Rhodesia declared independence in 1965, Zambia's president Kenneth Kaunda and Tanzania's Julius Nyerere wanted a route through friendly land. The World Bank and Western governments said no. Mao Zedong's China agreed, with an interest-free loan.

Tens of thousands of Chinese and African workers built it, finishing ahead of time. It was China's largest aid project of the era and won it friends in Africa during the Cold War, when Beijing competed with both the West and the Soviet Union. The line later struggled with poor upkeep and falling traffic. Its story is often recalled in debates about the Belt and Road Initiative.
sum: The building of the TAZARA Railway by China between 1970 and 1975, a line of about 1,860 km from the copper belt of Zambia to the port of Dar es Salaam in Tanzania.
